raw_response:
The following are candidate mechanisms to investigate; transfer to the given Python runtime is an inference, and no integration or performance measurement was performed.

1. **PyPy type-version method cache** — https://docs.huihoo.com/pypy/2.6/interpreter-optimizations.html
   A cache keyed by lookup name, call site, and a type version could avoid repeated attribute lookup while type or base-class mutation invalidates the version.
   Constraint: Instance shadowing still needs checking; globals and builtins require coverage of their distinct mutation paths.
   Evidence timing: pre-decision, from the PyPy 2.6 documentation snapshot, corroborated by live primary documentation.

2. **SELF change-dependency lists** — https://bibliography.selflanguage.org/implementation.html
   Dependency lists from mutable bindings to compiled methods could shift work from each read to mutations that invalidate affected optimizations.
   Constraint: Requires complete mutation interception, dependency storage, and handling for active compiled frames.
   Evidence timing: pre-decision; the primary bibliography dates publication to 1989/1991.

3. **Java SwitchPoint** — https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/lang/invoke/SwitchPoint.html
   A SwitchPoint-style one-way guard could select a cached binding's fast path until rebinding switches dependent sites to a general lookup.
   Constraint: This JVM API is a design analogue; synchronization can be costly and renewed speculation needs a fresh switch point.
   Evidence timing: pre-decision; versioned Java SE 7 API, with the platform's July 2011 release confirmed by https://download.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se7/jls7.pdf.

4. **SELF polymorphic inline caches** — https://bibliography.selflanguage.org/pics.html
   Small per-site caches of multiple lookup outcomes could retain fast paths for recurring namespace or type states while misses return to generic lookup.
   Constraint: PICs alone do not detect rebinding: entries need validity guards, and many states increase test or miss costs.
   Evidence timing: pre-decision; ECOOP July 1991.

5. **PyPy module cell dictionaries** — https://docs.huihoo.com/pypy/2.6/config/objspace.std.withcelldict.html
   PyPy's module cell dictionaries are a concrete specialized-storage component to investigate for JIT-optimized global-name access.
   Constraint: Documentation requires a JIT and honor__builtins__=False; implementation-source retrieval failed, leaving the mutation-validation algorithm unverified.
   Evidence timing: pre-decision; the original project-documentation mirror identifies release-2.6.x and copyright 2015.

6. **Linux sequence counters** — https://docs.kernel.org/locking/seqlock.html
   Sequence counters offer an alternative mutation-validation pattern: readers compare generation values around a lookup and retry if a writer intervenes.
   Constraint: This is a synchronization analogue; writers need serialization, pointer lifetimes need protection, and retries may dominate.
   Evidence timing: unknown; this is live documentation without a verified historical version.

7. **JavaScriptCore property and global watchpoints** — https://webkit.org/blog/10308/
   Property and global watchpoints could let optimized code embed a binding and receive mutation-triggered invalidation instead of repeatedly checking the binding.
   Constraint: This evidence is from 2020; transfer requires complete write hooks and safe deoptimization of active code.
   Evidence timing: post-decision, published 2020-07-29.
